name: Colorado
basePeriod: The first four of the last five completed calendar quarters before your claim. Colorado can use the last four completed quarters if those do not qualify.
notModeled: Enter the quarters in order, earliest first: Colorado uses the highest two consecutive quarters.
A cap on how much of any one quarter counts toward the total, which changes it only when one quarter is far larger than the rest.

citation.sourceNote: C.R.S. 8-73-102: "sixty percent of one-twenty-sixth of the wages paid ... during the two consecutive quarters of the individual's base period in which such total wages were highest", rounded down; or, for a claimant at that maximum, "fifty percent of one fifty-second of his total wages", paid if greater. CDLE's estimator: the first "currently cannot exceed $804 per week, or be less than $25", the second "$884"; at least $2,500 in wages. 8-73-107: base-period wages of at least the greater of $2,500 or 40 times the rate. 8-73-104: the total is "twenty-six times his weekly benefit amount or one-third of his wage credits ... whichever is the lesser." No dependent allowance (a 2023 bill for one was lost). One unpaid waiting week. Read 2026-10-19.
